name: University of Iceland (Háskóli Íslands)
englishTestNote: IELTS or TOEFL required for English-taught graduate programs; check program-specific requirements
tuitionNote: Public — annual registration fee only (~75,000 ISK / ~500 EUR). No tuition for EU/EEA or international students at undergraduate level.
studentNotes: Iceland's oldest and largest university. Broadest program range — humanities through medicine. Most undergraduate programs taught in Icelandic; English-medium offerings concentrated at the graduate level. Acceptance ~80–89%.
accreditationBody: Ministry of Culture, Innovation and Higher Education (Iceland)

name: Reykjavík University (Háskólinn í Reykjavík)
englishTestNote: Many programs taught in English; IELTS/TOEFL required for non-native speakers
tuitionNote: Private — semester-based tuition fees (typically several thousand USD per semester depending on program). Confirm current rates with university.
studentNotes: Private non-profit founded 1998. Substantial English-medium offering across business, law, computer science and engineering. Stronger international student presence than the public Icelandic universities.
accreditationBody: Ministry of Culture, Innovation and Higher Education (Iceland)

name: University of Akureyri (Háskólinn á Akureyri)
englishTestNote: IELTS or TOEFL required for English-taught programs (notably nursing)
tuitionNote: Public — annual registration fee only (~75,000 ISK / ~500 EUR).
studentNotes: Public university in north Iceland (Akureyri, Iceland's second city). Notable for an English-medium nursing program — relevant for healthcare workers seeking Nordic credentials. Smaller than University of Iceland.
accreditationBody: Ministry of Culture, Innovation and Higher Education (Iceland)

name: Bifröst University
tuitionNote: Tuition-free following 2024 state funding agreements. Verify current arrangement with university.
studentNotes: Niche specialist institution — not a comprehensive university. Focus is business, law, and social sciences. Founded 1918 on the Ruskin College, Oxford model. Rural campus in Borgarfjörður (~100 km from Reykjavík). Included for honest coverage of Iceland's full accredited list, not as a general option.
accreditationBody: Ministry of Culture, Innovation and Higher Education (Iceland)

name: Iceland University of the Arts (Listaháskóli Íslands)
tuitionNote: Tuition-free following 2024 state funding agreements. Verify current arrangement with university.
studentNotes: Niche specialist institution — Iceland's only accredited arts university. Programs are strictly arts and design (fine arts, music, dance, theatre, design, architecture). Not a general university. Relevant for migrants specifically seeking arts/design credentials.
accreditationBody: Ministry of Culture, Innovation and Higher Education (Iceland)

name: Agricultural University of Iceland (Landbúnaðarháskóli Íslands)
englishTestNote: IELTS/TOEFL required for English-taught programs (limited at this institution)
tuitionNote: Public — annual registration fee only (~75,000 ISK / ~500 EUR).
studentNotes: Niche specialist institution — not a comprehensive university. Focused on agriculture, environment, and rural planning. Very small (~200 students). Rural campus in Hvanneyri. Included for honest coverage of Iceland's accredited list; relevant only for migrants specifically seeking agricultural or environmental science credentials.
accreditationBody: Ministry of Culture, Innovation and Higher Education (Iceland)

name: Hólar University (Háskólinn á Hólum)
englishTestNote: Some English at graduate level; verify program-specific
tuitionNote: Public — annual registration fee only (~75,000 ISK / ~500 EUR).
studentNotes: Niche specialist institution — not a comprehensive university. Smallest accredited Icelandic university. Programs are limited to aquaculture, equine science, and rural tourism. Site has historical roots to 1106; institutional university status since 2007. Included for honest coverage of Iceland's accredited list; relevant only for migrants specifically seeking these specialized fields.
accreditationBody: Ministry of Culture, Innovation and Higher Education (Iceland)

name: University of Copenhagen (Københavns Universitet)
englishTestNote: IELTS or TOEFL required for English-taught programs; many Master's and PhD programs taught in English
tuitionNote: Free for EU/EEA students. Non-EU/EEA tuition typically €8,000–€15,000 per year depending on program.
studentNotes: Founded 1479 — Denmark's oldest and largest university, second-oldest in Scandinavia. 38,000+ students, 200+ study programs across all major fields including medicine, law, theology, and natural sciences. Ranks among the top 100 universities globally per QS. Major destination for international healthcare and research migrants.
accreditationBody: Danmarks Akkrediteringsinstitution (Danish Accreditation Institution)

name: Aarhus University (Aarhus Universitet)
englishTestNote: IELTS or TOEFL required; 50+ Bachelor's and Master's programs offered in English; all PhD programs in English
tuitionNote: Free for EU/EEA students. Non-EU/EEA tuition typically €8,000–€14,800 per year.
studentNotes: Founded 1928. Comprehensive research university with main campus in Aarhus and additional facilities in Copenhagen, Roskilde, Silkeborg, Foulum, and Herning. Approximately 12% of students are international, drawn from 120 countries. Ranks among the top 150 globally.
accreditationBody: Danmarks Akkrediteringsinstitution (Danish Accreditation Institution)

name: University of Southern Denmark (Syddansk Universitet)
englishTestNote: IELTS or TOEFL required for English-taught programs; substantial English-medium offering at Master's level
tuitionNote: Free for EU/EEA students. Non-EU/EEA tuition typically €6,500–€13,500 per year.
studentNotes: Founded 1998 through merger of Odense University (founded 1966), the Southern Denmark School of Business and Engineering, and the South Jutland University Centre. Main campus in Odense; additional campuses in Kolding, Esbjerg, Sønderborg, Slagelse, and Copenhagen. Affiliated with Odense University Hospital (OUH) for clinical training.
accreditationBody: Danmarks Akkrediteringsinstitution (Danish Accreditation Institution)

name: Roskilde University (Roskilde Universitet)
englishTestNote: IELTS or TOEFL required for English-taught programs
tuitionNote: Free for EU/EEA students. Non-EU/EEA tuition typically €7,500–€15,000 per year.
studentNotes: Founded 1972. Smaller research university east of central Roskilde, distinctive for its problem-oriented, project-based interdisciplinary teaching model (tværfaglige studier). Programs span four areas: humanities, humanistic technologies, social sciences, and natural sciences.
accreditationBody: Danmarks Akkrediteringsinstitution (Danish Accreditation Institution)

name: Aalborg University (Aalborg Universitet)
englishTestNote: IELTS or TOEFL required for English-taught programs; English-medium offering strong at Master's level
tuitionNote: Free for EU/EEA students. Non-EU/EEA tuition typically €8,000–€14,000 per year.
studentNotes: Founded 1974. Headquartered in Aalborg with additional campuses in Copenhagen and Esbjerg. Internationally recognized for its Problem-Based Learning (PBL) pedagogical model. Strong emphasis on engineering, IT, and applied research. Notable destination for South Asian engineering and IT migrants.
accreditationBody: Danmarks Akkrediteringsinstitution (Danish Accreditation Institution)

name: Technical University of Denmark (Danmarks Tekniske Universitet)
englishTestNote: IELTS or TOEFL required; majority of Master's programs taught in English
tuitionNote: Free for EU/EEA students. Non-EU/EEA tuition typically €13,500–€16,000 per year (verify current rates).
studentNotes: Subject-focused: engineering and applied sciences only — not a comprehensive university. Founded 1829 by physicist H.C. Ørsted. Located in Kongens Lyngby, a Copenhagen suburb. Among Europe's top technical universities; ranks in the global top 100 for engineering. Approximately 20% of scientific staff recruited internationally. Major destination for South Asian engineering migrants.
accreditationBody: Danmarks Akkrediteringsinstitution (Danish Accreditation Institution)

name: Copenhagen Business School (CBS)
englishTestNote: IELTS or TOEFL required; substantial English-medium offering at Bachelor's and Master's levels
tuitionNote: Free for EU/EEA students. Non-EU/EEA tuition varies by program (verify with university).
studentNotes: Subject-focused: business, finance, economics, and management only — not a comprehensive university. Founded 1917. Located in Frederiksberg (Copenhagen). 22,000+ students, making it one of Europe's largest business schools. Globally recognized MBA program. Strong fit for migrants pursuing business or finance credentials.
accreditationBody: Danmarks Akkrediteringsinstitution (Danish Accreditation Institution)

name: IT University of Copenhagen (IT-Universitetet i København)
englishTestNote: IELTS or TOEFL required; substantial English-medium offering at Master's level
tuitionNote: Free for EU/EEA students. Non-EU/EEA tuition typically €12,500–€14,000 per year.
studentNotes: Subject-focused: information technology only (computer science, software development, data science, digital design, business IT) — not a comprehensive university. Founded 1999. Public autonomous university located in Copenhagen. Strong fit for migrants pursuing software, data, or digital-design credentials.
accreditationBody: Danmarks Akkrediteringsinstitution (Danish Accreditation Institution)
